statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-116333 (PostgreSQL parallel B-tree array scan reads beyond array bounds) affects only PostgreSQL 17 and 18. The PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116333/, says "Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected" and lists 18.7 and 17.12 as the fixed releases. The flaw is that the backends in a parallel B-tree scan with array keys hand their positions in the arrays to each other through shared memory (btps_arrElems) and use them without a range check. That exchange was added by commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/5bf748b86bc6786a3fc57fc7ce296c37da6564b0 ("Enhance nbtree ScalarArrayOp execution"), which is in the REL_17_0 tag and not on the PostgreSQL 16 branch; it also replaced _bt_parallel_advance_array_keys() with _bt_parallel_primscan_schedule(). The fix on the REL_17_STABLE branch, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/4cd18df09917c856b79615dfa23aa4cd5ee7c23d, carries the trailer "Security: CVE-2026-116333" and "Backpatch-through: 17", and changes only src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c. At every PostgreSQL 16 release this owner publishes, REL_16_13 through REL_16_16, the shared parallel B-tree scan state holds only a count of processed array keys (btps_arrayKeyCount) and no array element positions, so no backend indexes its own arrays with a position saved by another; see for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_16_16/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql16 at 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0. In every one of those builds the postgres server binary, usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in the postgresql16 package, reports its 16.x release on both architectures, contains the symbol name _bt_parallel_advance_array_keys and does not contain _bt_parallel_primscan_schedule; the same byte search finds _bt_parallel_primscan_schedule in the postgres binary of the postgresql17 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 builds on both architectures. None of the Alpine patches applied in the 16.16-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, touch the B-tree access method. Alpine's postgresql16 16.16-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116333, but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 16 outside the affected range.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116333 (PostgreSQL parallel B-tree array scan reads beyond array bounds) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.12 for the 17 major version: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116333/ and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch is the upgrade to 17.12 and lists CVE-2026-116333 under its secfixes; see https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-116333. The DHI postgresql17 17.12-r0 build for Alpine 3.23 is built from that APKBUILD, and its postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on both x86_64 and aarch64. Every earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0) reports an older 17.x release, so it is affected; 17.12-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-116333, a buffer over-read in parallel B-tree array scans that lets an object creator read chosen server memory addresses, in 17.12 (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116333/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116333, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/). Upstream lists only the 17 and 18 major versions as affected; within 17, releases before 17.12 are affected. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
